text:
maria: Heads-up — Aurora-Mini launches tomorrow 10:00 UTC. Quick infra check: perf tests from staging suggest ~1.6–1.9x token/sec vs current smallest model. Planning a gradual rollout but want to confirm fleet impact and regional constraints. Any obvious blockers?

aj: Do we have a GPU-hour estimate for steady-state at 100k sessions/day if routed 100% to H100s?

maria: Rough back-of-envelope: if avg session = 1.2k tokens and model yields ~140 tokens/sec on H100, that's ~8.5 GPU-seconds per session. At 100k sessions/day -> ~236 GPU-hours/day -> ~1652 GPU-hours/week. That's without optimizations (batching, cache).

sanjay: I ran a simulator with prefix caching enabled and smart batching; numbers drop ~25%. So realistic target is ~1240 GPU-hours/week assuming 80% uptime and some headroom.

kim: Note: eu-west H100 reserved pool is 92% used this month. If traffic bursts route there we'll hit quotas. Suggest split: 30% eu-west -> p4d fallback (latency delta ~+20ms), 70% us-west H100. Also watch inter-region egress costs.

maria: Good call. If we split like that, expected global GPU-hours shift: H100(us) ~1150/wk, p4d(eu) ~300/wk.

aj: Packing constraints: Aurora-Mini mem footprint is ~22GB per replica after quantization. On our h100.2 nodes we can only place 2 per node reliably (OOM margin). That increases node count vs other models.

sanjay: Ops test: `kubectl get pods -n inference | grep aurora-mini`
```
# example output from canary
aurora-mini-5bb7f   1/1   Running   0     18m
aurora-mini-5bb7f   1/1   Running   0     12m
```

kim: Canary saw CPU networking spikes in us-west at 5% traffic earlier — some retries from the routing layer. Might be connection churn from p99 client latencies. Recommending connection pool tuning on the gateway. :eyes:

maria: Ops, can we get a quick network check and confirm no egress ACL rate-limiting in us-west?

oncall-ops: Checking. Current egress ACLs: no hard rate-limits, but observed short TCP resets during last canary window correlated with autoscaler churn. Increasing pod readiness probe window reduced resets in staging.

aj: On the cost side — with the regional split, incremental infra cost delta compared to baseline (old small model) is approx: +$12k/week (H100 run-rate) + extra node overhead ~ $1.5k/week. These are infra-only, not per-token billing.

sanjay: We should also model worst-case holiday traffic (x1.6) and have a temporary reserved pool capacity plan. If holiday hits and routing keeps 70/30, eu-west p4d will saturate quickly. Recommend burst policy to spill to shared dedicated pool with automatic fallback to smaller quantized variant.

maria: Action items: 1) eng-infra to pre-scale H100 node pool by +15% in us-west by 06:00 UTC tomorrow. 2) infra to create p4d fallback capacity in eu-west with auto-burst. 3) platform to apply gateway connection pool tuning and extend readiness probe for canary pods. 4) finance to confirm short-term budget for estimated +$15k/week delta.

kim: I'll own #1 and #2. Will open a capacity ticket with exact node counts.

oncall-ops: I'll apply the readiness probe change to the canary template and monitor for TCP reset rate for next 2 hours.

aj: I'll update the cost sheet and produce a 72h burn projection including holiday x1.6 scenario.

maria: Thanks — will wait for tickets. If canary stays green we'll start a 24h linear ramp at 12:00 UTC tomorrow. :thumbsup:
